Record date: 2129-07-10
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 07/10/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening shortness of breath, persistent cough with increased sputum production, and continued bilateral lower extremity edema.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after one week of treatment for his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation and congestive heart failure. He reports no significant improvement in his respiratory symptoms despite adherence to the prescribed prednisone and azithromycin regimen. He continues to experience substantial shortness of breath at rest and with minimal exertion. His cough has become more frequent and productive, with increased greenish sputum and occasional blood-tinged secretions. He notes that he has utilized his albuterol inhaler excessively, averaging 20 times per day, indicating inadequate control of his symptoms.
Additionally, the patient reports that his bilateral lower extremity edema has persisted, with notable discomfort and pain, particularly when standing or walking. He has been compliant with the increased furosemide dosage; however, he has not noticed any significant reduction in fluid retention. His insomnia remains unresolved, with anxiety exacerbating his inability to achieve restful sleep.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, - weight gain, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + worsening shortness of breath, + increased productive cough with greenish sputum, + hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 150/90 mmHg - Heart Rate: 92 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 24 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 87% on room air
General: The patient appears in moderate respiratory distress, using accessory muscles to aid in breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring, oropharynx clear.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally with notable wheezing; crackles are prominent in the lower lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Extremities: Persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, with pitting noted, particularly in the thighs.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation, with inadequate response to current treatment. 2. Congestive heart failure, with persistent fluid overload and worsening edema. 3. Insomnia exacerbated by anxiety and respiratory distress, with little improvement.
PLAN
1. Discontinue oral corticosteroids (prednisone) as the patient has not demonstrated sufficient improvement and consider a short course of intravenous corticosteroids if symptoms do not stabilize. 2. Change antibiotic therapy to levofloxacin 750 mg daily for 5 days, given the patient's increased sputum production and hemoptysis, to address possible bacterial superinfection. 3. Initiate continuous nebulized albuterol treatments every 2 hours and consider adding nebulized budesonide every 6 hours to reduce airway inflammation. 4. Further increase furosemide dosage to 120 mg daily, and consider adding spironolactone 25 mg daily to manage fluid retention and enhance diuresis. 5. Schedule an echocardiogram to assess cardiac function and rule out any underlying cardiac causes of the patient's edema and dyspnea. 6. Refer to a pulmonologist for advanced management of COPD and potential consideration for pulmonary rehabilitation. 7. Continue to discuss cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia and consider a trial of a low-dose sedative-hypnotic medication if non-pharmacological strategies are ineffective.
The patient was educated on the revised treatment plan, including the importance of medication adherence and monitoring for any worsening symptoms. He expressed understanding and willingness to comply with the new recommendations.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was stable for discharge with a follow-up appointment scheduled for 07/17/29. He was advised to seek immediate medical attention if he experiences increased difficulty breathing, chest pain, or any new concerning symptoms.
